question_text: Which government agency is the central personnel agency of the Philippine government?

hint_ladder.title: Hanapin ang 'personnel'
hint_ladder.text: Ang tanong ay tungkol sa ahensiyang namamahala sa mga empleyado ng gobyerno, hindi sa pera o boto.

hint_ladder.title: Tatlong Commission, Iba-iba
hint_ladder.text: May tatlong Constitutional Commission: CSC para sa tao, COA para sa pera, COMELEC para sa boto. Ang keyword: 'personnel' = tao.

hint_ladder.title: Gamitin ang scenario
hint_ladder.text: Kunwari nasa barangay ka: COA nag-audit ng budget, COMELEC naghahanda ng eleksyon, DILG nagbabantay sa LGU. Sino humahawak ng hiring? CSC lang 'yan!

hint_ladder.title: CSC = Civil Service
hint_ladder.text: Ang sagot ay yung may 'Civil Service' sa pangalan. Sila ang nangangasiwa ng exam, appointment, at disiplina ng civil servants.

A.text: You might have chosen A because COA is a constitutional commission, but it audits money, not personnel.

B.text: You might have chosen B because COMELEC also a commission, but it handles elections, not civil service.

C.text: Correct. CSC, the Civil Service Commission, is the central personnel agency managing government employees' careers.

D.text: You might have chosen D because DILG oversees local governments, but it's a department, not a commission, and not for personnel.

next_time_rule: Pag 'central personnel agency,' isipin 'CSC'—Careers, Serbisyo, Civil servants. COA=Check, COMELEC=Count, DILG=Districts.
deconstruct_text:
Imagine nasa barangay hall ka, nag-aasikaso ng payroll ng mga kagawad. May magtatanong: 'Sino ba ang central personnel agency?' Syempre, ang iniisip mo ay sino nagma-manage ng tao—hindi pera, hindi boto, at hindi local government unit.

Ang CSC ang central personnel agency. Ito ay isa sa tatlong Constitutional Commissions: CSC = Careers at Serbisyo sibil; COA = Check ng Accounts; COMELEC = Count ng boto. DILG naman ay department para sa local government. Remember: personnel = tao, kaya CSC.
